key_insight: GUI-Libra improves long-horizon GUI navigation by combining action-aware supervised reasoning with a partially verifiable RL scheme, aligning chain-of-thought with concrete UI actions so reasoning helps—not hurts—grounding.
problem_solved: Open-source native GUI agents fail on long-horizon tasks because training data lack action-aligned reasoning and standard post-training pipelines (CoT SFT and step-wise RL) either break grounding or suffer from partial verifiability and poor credit assignment.
method: Action-aware supervision: generate or curate reasoning traces that are explicitly aligned to concrete GUI actions so the model's internal rationale maps to verifiable steps.

Partially verifiable RL: structure reinforcement learning around verifiable subgoals or checks (hybrid supervised + RL updates) to reduce spurious credit assignment when full verification is impossible.
Pipeline redesign: avoid vanilla CoT fine-tuning that detaches reasoning from actions and instead combine action-grounded SFT with constrained/verified RL updates for stability.
impact: Makes open-source GUI agents more reliable and interpretable for long-horizon automation (e.g., testing, task automation, accessibility) by improving grounding between reasoning and actions and stabilizing RL fine-tuning.

paper_title: GUI-Libra: Training Native GUI Agents to Reason and Act with Action-aware Supervision and Partially Verifiable RL
paper_authors: Rui Yang, Qianhui Wu, Zhaoyang Wang, Hanyang Chen, Ke Yang
